about: Example data for the SkillLens tour, generated by the real scoring engine. Not a real person.

results.name: Racket arm in the loaded position
results.headline: Needs about 10° less — a little
results.cue: Your arm is too straight behind you, so there is no whip left to release. Bend the elbow more in the load.

drills.name: Shadow smash with a pause
drills.purpose: Loading the racket arm behind your head and turning your side to the net.
steps: Stand side-on to the net, racket up.
Lift the racket behind your head with the elbow up and bent at about a right angle. Pause for 2 seconds.
Rotate your chest to the net and swing through, finishing across your body.

results.name: Reach at contact
results.headline: Needs about 8° more — a little
results.cue: You are hitting with a bent arm, so the shuttle leaves flat instead of steeply downwards. Reach up and take it at full stretch.

drills.name: Highest-point contact
drills.purpose: Hitting the shuttle at full stretch, for a steeper smash.
steps: Hang a shuttle on a string just above your full overhead reach, or have a partner hold one up.
Shadow-smash and touch the shuttle with the racket at full arm extension.
Raise it a little once you can reach it every time.

results.name: Racket arm speed
results.headline: Needs about 115°/s more — a little
results.cue: Your arm speed is on the low side. Stay loose — in badminton the speed comes from a relaxed forearm snap, not from muscling it.

drills.name: Forearm snap with the cover on
drills.purpose: A loose, fast forearm and wrist snap.
steps: Put the head cover on your racket for a little extra air resistance.
From the loaded position, swing through with a relaxed grip and let the forearm snap over.
Listen for the whoosh; a louder whoosh means a faster snap.
drills.equipment: A racket with a head cover
drills.safety: Keep the grip loose. Stop if your elbow or shoulder hurts.

results.name: Leg load before the jump
results.headline: Needs about 3° less — a touch
results.cue: You are sinking very deep, which slows you down for the next shot.

drills.name: Scissor-kick jumps
drills.purpose: Loading your legs and springing up, with the hips turning first.
steps: Start side-on with your racket-side leg back.
Bend your legs, jump, and swap legs in the air like a scissor.
Turn your hips first, then your shoulders, then swing. Land balanced.
drills.safety: Land with soft knees. Skip if your knees or ankles hurt.

results.name: Hips before shoulders

results.name: Hips and chest rising together
results.headline: Needs about 28 ms less — a little
results.cue: Your hips are shooting up before your chest, which turns the squat into a good-morning and loads the lower back. Drive your chest and hips up together.

drills.name: Box squats
drills.purpose: Reaching the right depth every time, with hips and chest rising together.
steps: Put a box or bench behind you at a height where your thighs are about level with the floor when you sit.
Squat down until you just touch it, without dropping onto it.
Stand up with your chest and hips rising at the same speed. Raise or lower the box to adjust depth.

drills.name: Tempo squats
drills.purpose: A controlled squat with both legs working evenly.
steps: Bodyweight only. Take 3 seconds to go down, pause 1 second, and take 1 second to come up.
Watch your knees in a mirror: they should track over your toes, both the same.
Keep your weight even across both feet.

results.name: Lower-back rounding
results.headline: Needs about 4° less — a touch
results.cue: Your lower back is rounding at the bottom — the move lifters call 'butt wink'. This is the highest-risk fault in the squat. Go less deep and brace your middle before you descend.

drills.name: Goblet squats with a pause
drills.purpose: A tall chest and a flat lower back at the bottom.
steps: Hold a light weight, a bag or a water bottle against your chest.
Squat down, keeping your chest up and back flat, and pause 2 seconds at the bottom.
Stand up slowly. Stop going lower at the point your lower back starts to round.
